_readme: The hub's running order. Same fleet as tools.json, grouped by the job
someone came to do rather than by industry, and written for someone who
does not already know what DICOM or a distro is.
Every tool in tools.json belongs in exactly one group here — this is the
hub, and a tool it does not list is a tool nobody can find. The order of
the groups is the order of the page, and the ones that genuinely need a
technical reader go last and say so.
'ref' is the tool's exact name in tools.json — that is where the url, the icon
and the local flag come from, so a moved subdomain is still one edit in one
file. A ref that matches nothing is skipped rather than rendered broken.
'plain' is what the tool DOES, in the words of someone who does not know what
it is called. 'line' is one sentence under it. Both are English keys — add
each to the four locales in i18n.js or the page falls back to English.
'shot' is optional: a screenshot at assets/shots/<file>.webp, shown instead of
the icon plate. A real picture of the tool beats any glyph for a first-time
visitor, so fill these in as they are captured.
